collocation.en: [statement], you know, + [the word or phrase you can't recall]

contexts.en: Casual conversation when you can't recall a word mid-sentence

connotation.en: informal, friendly, invites listener to fill in

example.en: I need to pick up the, you know, the thing you use to open wine bottles.

collocation.en: [forgotten name], what's it called, + [attempted description]

contexts.en: Everyday chat when a name escapes you

example.en: We went to what's it called, that little café behind the station.

expression: it's on the tip of my tongue

collocation.en: [almost remembered word] is on the tip of my tongue

contexts.en: When you almost remember a name or word but can't quite get it

example.en: Her name is... ugh, it's on the tip of my tongue. Give me a second.

collocation.en: [description of concept]. What's the word for + [the exact term you can't recall]?

contexts.en: Describing a concept when the exact term isn't coming

example.en: There's the word for when someone helps you without being asked... altruism?

collocation.en: [situation or object], what do you call it, + [halting description]

contexts.en: Pausing mid-story to search for vocabulary

example.en: She did that thing where—what do you call it—she gaslit me about the whole situation.

collocation.en: [incomplete statement], um, + [brief pause before continuing]

contexts.en: The most universal filler—dropped into any conversation when searching for a word

example.en: The restaurant was, um, you know that place with the red awning on Fifth?

collocation.en: Well, + [pause] + [attempted answer]

contexts.en: When someone asks you a question and you need a moment to form an answer

example.en: Well, I haven't really thought about it that way before.

collocation.en: Let me see... + [pause] + [retrieved fact or opinion]

contexts.en: When asked for an opinion or fact you need to retrieve

example.en: Let me see... I think the last time we spoke was back in March.

collocation.en: Hmm, + [pause] + [thoughtful response]

contexts.en: When a question catches you off guard and you need to think

example.en: Hmm, that's a good question. I guess it depends on the context.

collocation.en: How shall I put it... + [carefully phrased statement]

contexts.en: When you need to phrase something delicately or precisely

example.en: How shall I put this—it wasn't a disaster, but it definitely wasn't great.

collocation.en: Give me a second, + [pause] + [formulated answer]

contexts.en: Straightforward request for thinking time in any conversation

example.en: Give me a second, I want to phrase this right.

collocation.en: That's an interesting question. + [pause] + [thoughtful answer]

contexts.en: When a thoughtful question deserves a thoughtful pause before answering

example.en: That's an interesting question—I've never really thought about it from that angle before.

collocation.en: [unclear statement], I mean, + [rephrased or softened version]

contexts.en: When you need to stall before delivering a sensitive point

example.en: I mean, it's not that I don't want to go, it's just that I'm exhausted.

collocation.en: The thing is, + [complicated or awkward explanation]

contexts.en: Leading into a potentially awkward or complicated explanation

example.en: The thing is, I've already made other plans for that weekend.

collocation.en: [tangent or digression]. Like I said, + [return to main point]

contexts.en: Recovering after a tangent, returning to your main point

example.en: Anyway, like I said, the whole trip was basically a comedy of errors.

collocation.en: [partial statement], actually, + [self-correction or backtrack]

contexts.en: Realising you need to backtrack or correct yourself mid-thought

example.en: Actually, wait—I'm getting my dates mixed up. It was Thursday, not Friday.

collocation.en: To be honest, + [candid or potentially unpopular truth]

contexts.en: Stalling before saying something potentially unpopular or too honest

example.en: To be honest, I haven't even started on that report yet.

collocation.en: [rambling lead-up]. So yeah, + [main takeaway or pivot]

contexts.en: Filling a gap while you collect your thoughts, often before pivoting

example.en: So yeah, I think the main takeaway is that we need better documentation.

collocation.en: [unclear statement], I mean, + [rephrased or softened version]

contexts.en: Correcting yourself in the middle of a story or explanation

example.en: We went to Barcelona—I mean, Valencia—last summer for the festival.

collocation.en: [initial statement], or rather, + [more accurate version]

contexts.en: Refining a statement to be more accurate

example.en: She's my colleague, or rather, she was my colleague before the restructure.

collocation.en: [partial statement], actually, + [self-correction or backtrack]

contexts.en: Stopping yourself mid-claim when you realise you're wrong

example.en: It was about two hundred—actually, no, it was closer to a hundred and fifty.

collocation.en: [awkward statement]. Let me rephrase that: + [clearer version]

contexts.en: When you realise what you said came out wrong or unclear

example.en: That sounded harsh. Let me rephrase that—I meant it as constructive feedback.

collocation.en: [misunderstood statement]. What I meant was + [clarified meaning]

contexts.en: Clarifying after someone misinterprets your words

example.en: What I meant was that the deadline is flexible, not that it doesn't matter.

collocation.en: [abandoned statement]. Scratch that, + [fresh attempt]

contexts.en: Abandoning what you just said to try again more clearly

example.en: Scratch that—I'm making this sound way more complicated than it actually is.

collocation.en: [complex statement]. In other words, + [simplified version]

contexts.en: Summarising a complex point more simply for clarity

example.en: The algorithm prioritises recency over relevance—in other words, newer posts win.

collocation.en: [original framing]. To put it another way, + [alternative framing]

contexts.en: Offering an alternative framing of the same idea

example.en: To put it another way, we're spending more than we're earning, and that can't last.

collocation.en: [vague statement], that is to say, + [more precise version]

contexts.en: Adding precision to a statement that was a bit vague

example.en: The proposal was rejected—that is to say, it was sent back for major revisions.

expression: what I'm trying to say is

collocation.en: [ramble or long explanation]. What I'm trying to say is + [core point]

contexts.en: When you've been rambling and need to get to the point

example.en: Look, what I'm trying to say is that I don't think this is working anymore.

collocation.en: [detailed explanation]. So essentially, + [boiled-down core]

contexts.en: Boiling down a complicated explanation to its core

example.en: So essentially, the update just makes everything run faster without changing the interface.

collocation.en: [first metaphor or framing]. To put it differently, + [new analogy or angle]

contexts.en: Trying a completely different metaphor to make a point land

example.en: To put it differently, think of the app as a house—the backend is the foundation, the UI is the paint job.

collocation.en: [complex situation]. Basically, + [stripped-down bottom line]

contexts.en: Stripping away complexity to give someone the bottom line

example.en: Basically, if you don't reply by Friday, they give your slot to someone else.

collocation.en: [long story or explanation]. In a nutshell, + [shortest possible summary]

contexts.en: Giving the shortest possible summary of a long story

example.en: In a nutshell, the meeting was two hours of people agreeing with each other.

collocation.en: [technical or complex issue]. Put simply, + [plain-language version]

contexts.en: Boiling a technical or complex issue down for non-experts

example.en: Put simply, the battery drains because too many apps run in the background.

expression: the long and short of it

collocation.en: [drawn-out story]. The long and short of it is + [bottom line]

contexts.en: Summarising a drawn-out story for someone who wants the bottom line

example.en: The long and short of it is that we're moving offices next month.

expression: at the end of the day

collocation.en: [detailed discussion]. At the end of the day, + [what ultimately matters]

contexts.en: Cutting through detail to focus on what ultimately matters

example.en: At the end of the day, what matters is whether the team can actually deliver on time.

collocation.en: [over-explanation]. Look, all I'm saying is + [stripped-down core point]

contexts.en: Stripping your point to its bare essence after over-explaining

example.en: Look, all I'm saying is that maybe we should get a second opinion before signing.

collocation.en: [point A]. Also, + [related point B]

contexts.en: Adding a related point in a casual chat or meeting

example.en: The hotel has a great pool. Also, they do free breakfast until eleven.

collocation.en: [main point]. In addition, + [further point of equal weight]

contexts.en: Layering another point in a semi-formal discussion

example.en: We need better onboarding. In addition, the team has asked for more regular feedback sessions.

collocation.en: [benefit or reason A]. Plus, + [additional benefit or reason B]

contexts.en: Piling on reasons or benefits in casual conversation

example.en: The rent includes utilities. Plus, it's walking distance from the office.

collocation.en: [supporting point A]. Moreover, + [weightier supporting point B]

contexts.en: Adding a weighty supporting point in a formal argument

example.en: The policy reduced emissions by fifteen percent. Moreover, it created thousands of green jobs.

collocation.en: [primary quality] as well as + [secondary quality]

contexts.en: Acknowledging a secondary benefit alongside the main point

example.en: The design is stunning as well as being highly functional.

collocation.en: [list item 1], [item 2], and also + [last-minute addition]

contexts.en: Casually piling on afterthoughts in informal conversation

example.en: We need milk, bread, eggs, and also—can you grab some of that sourdough from the bakery?

collocation.en: [impressive point A]. What's more, + [even more impressive point B]

contexts.en: Adding a surprising or impressive point on top of what you just said

collocation.en: [supporting argument A]. Furthermore, + [stronger supporting argument B]

contexts.en: Building a structured case with increasingly important points

example.en: The product is cheaper than competitors. Furthermore, independent tests show it lasts twice as long.

collocation.en: [striking point A]. Not only that, + [even more striking point B]

contexts.en: Emphasising an additional point in excited storytelling

example.en: He showed up late to the interview. Not only that, he hadn't even read the job description.

collocation.en: [bad thing A]. On top of that, + [additional bad thing B]

contexts.en: Adding a final point that makes a situation even more remarkable

collocation.en: [already bad situation]. To make matters worse, + [further complication]

contexts.en: Adding a negative detail to an already bad situation

collocation.en: [chain of unfortunate events]. And on top of all that, + [final straw]

contexts.en: Adding the final straw to a chain of unfortunate or remarkable events

example.en: The hotel was overbooked, the flight was delayed, and on top of all that, someone stole my wallet.

collocation.en: [current topic]. Incidentally, + [tangential but interesting fact]

contexts.en: Slipping in a related but tangential fact mid-conversation

collocation.en: [remark or observation]. Come to think of it, + [sudden realisation]

contexts.en: A sudden realisation or extra thought that just occurred to you

collocation.en: [main recommendation]. It's worth mentioning that + [important caveat or bonus]

collocation.en: [list of reminders]. Oh, and another thing — + [last-minute addition]

contexts.en: Remembering something else to add in an animated conversation

collocation.en: [outcome or change] due to + [formal reason or cause]

example.en: The event has been postponed due to unforeseen circumstances.

collocation.en: [positive outcome] thanks to + [person or contributing factor]

contexts.en: Acknowledging a person or thing that caused a positive outcome

example.en: Thanks to her last-minute edits, the proposal got approved on the first submission.

collocation.en: [small cause or event], which led to + [larger or cascading consequence]

collocation.en: [event or force] brought about + [significant change or transformation]

collocation.en: [observed outcome] — it must have been because + [speculated cause]

contexts.en: Guessing why something happened based on evidence

example.en: He missed the call—it must have been because his phone was on silent again.

collocation.en: [observed pattern], which suggests that + [logical inference]

contexts.en: Drawing a logical conclusion from observed facts

collocation.en: [known premise]. It stands to reason that + [logical conclusion]

contexts.en: Making a logical deduction everyone should agree with

collocation.en: [visible evidence]. Judging by + [inferred state or cause]

contexts.en: Inferring cause from visible cues or behaviour

example.en: Judging by how quiet she got, I think the news hit her harder than she let on.

collocation.en: [observed outcome], probably because + [educated guess at cause]

contexts.en: Making an educated guess about a cause in casual conversation

example.en: They didn't show up, probably because the invite went to their spam folder.

collocation.en: [puzzling outcome]. The likely explanation is that + [most reasonable cause]

contexts.en: Offering the most reasonable guess for why something happened

example.en: The likely explanation is that the supplier ran into production delays and didn't want to admit it.

collocation.en: [surface-level explanation]. The reason is + [deeper root cause]

contexts.en: Getting to the core explanation after dismissing surface-level ones

example.en: The reason we're behind isn't the budget—it's that we lost two senior devs.

collocation.en: [complex situation]. At the heart of it, + [fundamental cause]

contexts.en: Identifying the deepest or most fundamental cause

example.en: At the heart of it, the conflict comes down to misaligned incentives.

collocation.en: [current problem] stems from + [originating source or cause]

contexts.en: Tracing a current problem back to its origin

example.en: Most of the friction on the team stems from unclear role definitions.

collocation.en: [chain of events]. It all goes back to + [single originating decision or moment]

contexts.en: Tracing a complex situation to a single originating cause

example.en: It all goes back to that decision we made in January to delay the launch.

collocation.en: [surface symptom A, symptom B]. The underlying issue is + [true root problem]

contexts.en: Peeling back surface symptoms to reveal the real problem

example.en: The arguments about the schedule are just surface-level. The underlying issue is trust.

collocation.en: [visible dysfunction]. At the root of + [deepest originating cause]

contexts.en: Identifying the deepest originating cause after peeling back layers

example.en: At the root of the team's dysfunction was a total lack of psychological safety.

collocation.en: [thing A with trait X], whereas + [thing B with opposite trait Y]

contexts.en: Comparing two things side by side to highlight differences

example.en: The old system took five minutes to boot, whereas this one's ready in under ten seconds.

collocation.en: [advantage or argument A]. On the other hand, + [opposing disadvantage or argument B]

contexts.en: Presenting an opposing view in a balanced discussion

example.en: Remote work saves commute time. On the other hand, it can feel isolating.

collocation.en: [thing or situation A]. In contrast, + [starkly different thing or situation B]

contexts.en: Setting up a stark difference between two things

example.en: The city centre is chaotic and loud. In contrast, the suburbs are almost eerily quiet.

collocation.en: Unlike + [the norm or other examples], + [this specific case stands apart]

contexts.en: Singling something out as different from the norm

collocation.en: While + [conceding point A], + [contrasting main point B]

contexts.en: Juxtaposing two contrasting ideas in one sentence

example.en: While the design is beautiful, the user experience is frustratingly slow.

collocation.en: [scenario with trait X]. Conversely, + [opposite scenario with trait Y]

contexts.en: Flipping to the opposite scenario in a balanced comparison

example.en: Poor lighting makes a room feel cramped. Conversely, well-placed lamps can make a small space feel expansive.

collocation.en: Even though + [obstacle or counterpoint], + [action or result that happened regardless]

contexts.en: Acknowledging an obstacle before stating what happened anyway

example.en: Even though we were understaffed, we still shipped the update on time.

collocation.en: Despite + [obstacle or warning], + [action or result achieved against the odds]

contexts.en: Pointing out that something happened against the odds

example.en: Despite everyone telling her it was impossible, she got the funding in six weeks.

collocation.en: Admittedly, + [weakness or concession], + [but the overall point still stands]

contexts.en: Conceding a weakness before defending the overall point

example.en: Admittedly, the location isn't ideal, but the rent makes up for it.

collocation.en: Granted, + [conceded counterpoint], + [but the main argument still holds]

contexts.en: Accepting a counterpoint before pivoting back to your argument

example.en: Granted, the train takes longer than flying, but it's a third of the price.

collocation.en: [counterargument acknowledged]. All the same, + [sticking to original position]

contexts.en: Acknowledging the other side but sticking to your preference

example.en: I know it's the popular choice. All the same, I'd rather go somewhere less crowded.

collocation.en: [opponent's point acknowledged]. Be that as it may, + [position unchanged]

contexts.en: Acknowledging someone's point without letting it change your position

collocation.en: [earlier assumption]. Actually, + [contradicting discovery]

example.en: I was going to call a plumber. As it happens, my neighbour's brother is one.

collocation.en: [someone's stated position or warning]. Ironically, + [they fell victim to the very thing]

collocation.en: [expected pattern]. Oddly enough, + [counterintuitive finding]

contexts.en: Noting an unexpected or counterintuitive finding

collocation.en: [thing A with trait X], whereas + [thing B with opposite trait Y]

collocation.en: [thing A] is nowhere near as + [adjective] as + [thing B]

collocation.en: [new situation] involves considerably less + [negative quality] than + [old situation]

collocation.en: I see it differently — + [alternative perspective without dismissing theirs]

example.en: I see it a bit differently—I think the slow uptake is a messaging problem, not a product problem.

expression: that's one way to look at it

collocation.en: That's one way to look at it, but + [implying there's another valid perspective]

contexts.en: Acknowledging a perspective while implying there are others

example.en: That's one way to look at it, but the data tells a different story.

collocation.en: I'd argue the opposite — + [confidently taking the opposing view]

contexts.en: Directly but politely taking the opposing view

example.en: Actually, I'd argue the opposite—tight deadlines often produce the most creative solutions.

collocation.en: As we all know, + [shared background fact everyone in the room is aware of]

contexts.en: Referencing something everyone in the room is aware of

example.en: As we all know, the supplier has been unreliable for the past two quarters.

collocation.en: Obviously, + [point that should be clear to everyone present]

contexts.en: Pointing out something that should be clear to everyone

example.en: Obviously, we'd prefer to launch in spring, but the timeline doesn't allow it.

collocation.en: Needless to say, + [obvious reaction or outcome to a shared understanding]

contexts.en: Stating the obvious reaction to a situation

example.en: Needless to say, I was thrilled when they offered me the position.

collocation.en: It's no secret that + [something widely known but perhaps not openly discussed]

contexts.en: Acknowledging something widely known but perhaps not openly discussed

example.en: It's no secret that the team has been stretched thin since the reorganisation.

collocation.en: We've all been there — + [universal shared experience that builds empathy]

contexts.en: Appealing to a universal shared experience

example.en: We've all been there—you prepare for weeks and then your mind goes blank.

expression: if you see what I mean

collocation.en: [explanation], if you see what I mean — [checking if it landed]

contexts.en: Checking if your explanation landed during a casual chat

example.en: It's less of a job and more of a calling, if you see what I mean.

collocation.en: [explanation finished]. Does that make sense? — [pausing to check listener comprehension]

contexts.en: Pausing mid-explanation to ensure the listener is following

example.en: The data flows from the app to the server, then back. Does that make sense?

expression: are we on the same page

collocation.en: Are we on the same page about + [specific point being confirmed]?

contexts.en: Confirming alignment before moving forward in a discussion

example.en: Are we on the same page about the budget, or should we go over it again?

collocation.en: [informal description], you know what I mean? — [seeking informal confirmation]

contexts.en: Seeking confirmation that your informal description was understood

example.en: It's that feeling when you walk into a room and forget why—you know what I mean?

collocation.en: [your reasoning]. Does that track with + [the other person's understanding]?

contexts.en: Checking if your reasoning aligns with the other person's understanding

example.en: So the delay came from the design side, not engineering—if that tracks with what you saw.

collocation.en: Surprisingly, + [outcome that defied expectation]

contexts.en: Expressing pleasant or notable surprise at an outcome

example.en: Surprisingly, the cheapest option turned out to be the most durable.

collocation.en: I was taken aback by + [what genuinely caught you off guard]

contexts.en: Describing being genuinely caught off guard

example.en: I was taken aback by how thoughtful her feedback was—she'd really read the whole thing.

collocation.en: It never occurred to me that + [blind spot or unconsidered possibility]

contexts.en: Acknowledging a blind spot you didn't see coming

example.en: It never occurred to me that working from home could actually increase productivity.

collocation.en: [long search or expectation]. And lo and behold, + [dramatic surprising discovery]

contexts.en: Dramatically revealing a surprising discovery in a story

example.en: I searched everywhere for my keys, and lo and behold, they were in the fridge.

collocation.en: You won't believe + [surprising event or coincidence]

contexts.en: Building anticipation before sharing something surprising

example.en: You won't believe who I ran into at the airport—our old physics teacher.

collocation.en: Unfortunately, + [disappointing news delivered sympathetically]

contexts.en: Delivering disappointing news with a sympathetic tone

example.en: Unfortunately, the venue was double-booked, so we had to find an alternative.

collocation.en: I wish I had + [past action you regret not taking]

contexts.en: Expressing personal regret about a past decision

example.en: I wish I had started saving for retirement in my twenties instead of my thirties.

collocation.en: In hindsight, + [what you'd do differently with benefit of experience]

contexts.en: Reflecting on what you'd do differently with the benefit of experience

example.en: In hindsight, we should have tested the feature with real users before the full launch.

collocation.en: If only + [missed opportunity expressed wistfully]

contexts.en: Expressing wistful regret about missing an opportunity

example.en: If only I'd known they were hiring, I would have applied in a heartbeat.

collocation.en: It's a shame + [disappointing situation beyond anyone's control]

contexts.en: Expressing disappointment about a situation beyond anyone's control

example.en: It's a shame they couldn't make it—they would have loved the exhibit.

collocation.en: Frankly, + [candid statement even when uncomfortable]

contexts.en: Being completely honest, even when it's uncomfortable

example.en: Frankly, I think we've been avoiding the real problem for months.

collocation.en: Honestly, + [genuine sincere answer rather than a made-up one]

contexts.en: Answering with genuine candour rather than making something up

example.en: Honestly, I have no idea how they pulled it off with that budget.

collocation.en: To tell you the truth, + [revealing true feelings after perhaps hiding them]

contexts.en: Revealing your true feelings after perhaps hiding them

example.en: To tell you the truth, I was terrified the whole time I was on stage.

collocation.en: I'll be straight with you — + [honest but possibly unwelcome truth]

contexts.en: Preparing someone for an honest but possibly unwelcome truth

example.en: I'll be straight with you—the timeline you're proposing isn't realistic.

collocation.en: In all honesty, + [admitting something you might have been reluctant to say]

contexts.en: Admitting something you might have been reluctant to say

example.en: In all honesty, I expected the project to fail, and I'm thrilled I was wrong.

collocation.en: Can I just say — + [polite interjection in a group conversation]

contexts.en: Politely interjecting in a group conversation

example.en: Can I just say—I think what Sarah just proposed is actually brilliant.

collocation.en: If I could jump in here, + [polite interruption with a contribution]

contexts.en: Interrupting politely in a professional discussion

example.en: If I could jump in here, I have some data that might inform this decision.

collocation.en: That's interesting — + [building on someone's point while taking the floor]

contexts.en: Building on someone's point while taking the conversational floor

example.en: That's interesting—and it also connects to what we discussed about retention last week.

collocation.en: To add to + [point just made], + [extending or contributing further]

contexts.en: Contributing to the conversation by extending someone's point

example.en: To add to that, I think the timing issue is also about seasonal demand patterns.

collocation.en: [topic keyword just mentioned]. Speaking of which, + [natural segue to take the floor]

contexts.en: Using a natural segue to take the floor

example.en: Speaking of which, I actually tried that method you recommended and it worked perfectly.

collocation.en: Before I forget, + [final point added before yielding the floor]

contexts.en: Keeping the floor to add a final point before yielding

example.en: Before I forget, there's one more thing I wanted to mention about the schedule.

collocation.en: Let me finish + [this thought], + [then I'll yield the floor]

contexts.en: Assertively keeping the floor when someone tries to interrupt

example.en: Let me finish this thought, and then I want to hear your take.

collocation.en: [striking point A]. Not only that, + [even more striking point B]

contexts.en: Extending your point to hold the floor for another sentence

example.en: The design is elegant. Not only that, it actually improved load times by thirty percent.

collocation.en: [point A made]. The other thing is + [point B added without yielding floor]

contexts.en: Transitioning to a second point without yielding the floor

example.en: The other thing is, we haven't factored in the cost of customer support for the new feature.

collocation.en: Hang on, I'm getting to that — + [asking for patience before revealing the answer]

contexts.en: Playfully telling someone to wait for the answer to their question

example.en: Hang on, I'm getting to that—let me set the context first.

collocation.en: [your opinion stated]. What do you think? — [direct invitation to the other person]

contexts.en: Directly inviting someone else into the conversation

example.en: I've laid out my thinking. What do you think about the timeline?

expression: but I'd love to hear your take

collocation.en: [your perspective shared]. But I'd love to hear your take — [gracefully yielding the floor]

contexts.en: Gracefully yielding the floor after sharing your opinion

example.en: That's my perspective, but I'd love to hear your take on it.

collocation.en: Anyway, that's my side — + [signalling you've finished and it's their turn]

contexts.en: Signalling you've finished and it's someone else's turn

example.en: Anyway, that's my side of things. What's been going on with you?

collocation.en: I'll stop there and + [consciously opening the floor to others]

contexts.en: Consciously ending your contribution to make space for others

example.en: I've been talking for a while—I'll stop there and open it up to the group.

collocation.en: Over to you — + [formally handing the conversational floor to someone else]

contexts.en: Formally handing the conversational floor to someone else

example.en: That covers the main updates from my side. Over to you for any questions.
